title: Deep muscles of the anterior forearm (anterior)
lab: Forearm, Cubital Fossa, and Elbow Joint
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Proximal three quarters of the anterior and medial surfaces of the ulna and the interosseous membrane.
Bases of the distal phalanges of digits 2 to 5.
Lateral half (digits 2 and 3): anterior interosseous branch of the median nerve. Medial half (digits 4 and 5): ulnar nerve.
Flexes the distal interphalangeal joints of digits 2 to 5. Helps flex the other joints of the fingers and the wrist.
Anterior surface of the radius and the adjacent interosseous membrane.
Base of the distal phalanx of the thumb.
Anterior interosseous branch of the median nerve (C8, T1).
Flexes the thumb, mainly at its interphalangeal joint.
hy: With an anterior interosseous nerve lesion the tips of the thumb and index finger cannot be flexed, so the patient cannot make the OK sign.

rows: Distal quarter of the anterior surface of the ulna.
Distal quarter of the anterior surface of the radius.
Anterior interosseous branch of the median nerve (C8, T1).
Pronates the forearm. Holds the distal ends of the radius and ulna together.
Lateral epicondyle of the humerus, the radial collateral and annular ligaments, and the supinator crest of the ulna.
Lateral, posterior and anterior surfaces of the proximal third of the radius.
Deep branch of the radial nerve.
hy: The deep branch of the radial nerve passes through supinator and leaves it as the posterior interosseous nerve. Compression here causes finger drop without wrist drop and without sensory loss.

rows: Distal half of the anterior surface of the humerus.
Coronoid process and tuberosity of the ulna.
Musculocutaneous nerve (C5, C6). A small lateral part is supplied by the radial nerve.
Flexes the elbow in every position of the forearm.
